mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota GR Yaris engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Toyota GR Yaris G16E-GTS engine replacement typically costs £3,500-£5,500 for a used unit, £5,995-£8,500 for a reconditioned engine, and £5,995-£10,995 for a fully rebuilt unit (supply only). Fitting adds approximately £2,148 in labour (20 hours at specialist rates). Total fitted cost for a rebuilt engine typically ranges from £8,143 to £13,143.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of G16E-GTS engine failure in a Toyota GR Yaris?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common warning signs include sudden loss of power (boost solenoid failure), coolant loss or overheating (water pump or cooling system issues), unusual knocking noises (potential piston or bearing failure), and misfiring or rough running.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota GR Yaris?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Toyota GR Yaris worth £26,500-£61,750, a rebuilt G16E-GTS engine (£5,995-£10,995 supply) is almost always a sound investment. The GR Yaris is a modern classic-in-the-making, and the engine is central to its value and character. A quality rebuilt unit with upgraded components and warranty offers better long-term value than scrapping the car.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota GR Yaris engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Toyota GR Yaris G16E-GTS engine replacement typically takes 18-22 hours for a specialist workshop. Supply-only delivery takes 1-2 days, and supply & fit typically requires 3-5 working days total, depending on workshop availability.

mainEntity.name: Is the Toyota GR Yaris G16E-GTS engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The G16E-GTS is generally reliable in standard form when properly maintained. However, it's a highly stressed engine - producing over 170bhp per litre - and track use or aggressive tuning can push it beyond its limits. Common issues include boost solenoid failure (cheap fix), water pump leaks, and - in extreme cases - piston failure. Toyota revised pistons for the Gen 2 model.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Gen 1 and Gen 2 GR Yaris engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Gen 2 G16E-GTS (2024 onwards) produces 276bhp (up from 257bhp) and 288lb ft of torque. It features a stronger valvetrain, new exhaust valve material, increased fuel injection pressure and stronger pistons. The cooling system was also upgraded with an additional sub-radiator and an intercooler water spray system. Toyota revised the piston part number for Gen 2.

commonProblems.h2: Toyota GR Yaris - What It Costs to Fix, and When Replacement Makes Sense
commonProblems.h3: *TAG: * Common Problems *H2: * Toyota GR Yaris Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement *H3 (intro): * The Toyota GR Yaris G16E-GTS engine is a masterpiece of compact performance engineering - a bespoke 1.6-litre turbocharged three-cylinder that punches well above its weight. However, it's also a highly stressed engine pushing over 170bhp per litre, and track use, aggressive tuning, or missed maintenance can push it beyond its limits. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Piston Failure - Why the Toyota GR Yaris G16E-GTS Engine Can Suffer Catastrophic Damage
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 35,000-75,000 miles (higher risk with track use or tuning)
problems.rootCause: The G16E-GTS's pistons appear to be one of the engine's less robust components. Catastrophic failures - where a piston separates from the connecting rod and punches holes through the engine block - have been documented. These failures are typically associated with aggressive tuning, oil or fuel starvation, or sustained track use at the limit. Toyota revised the pistons for the Gen 2 GR Yaris (part number 13101-18040) and further revisions followed for later GR Corolla models.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When internal damage has occurred; often the most cost-effective route for a high-performance engine

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace bottom-end only; reuse cylinder head if undamaged
repairOptions.longevity: If head is salvageable and failure is confined to bottom-end

problems.h4: Boost Solenoid Failure - Why the Toyota GR Yaris G16E-GTS Loses Boost
problems.rootCause: The inline-three cylinder configuration generates vibration that can kill the OEM boost solenoid mounted on the engine. When the solenoid fails, the car loses boost and effectively becomes a naturally aspirated engine - still drivable but significantly down on power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace OEM or aftermarket solenoid, relocate away from engine if using aftermarket
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for all owners experiencing boost loss

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Only if internal damage has occurred
repairOptions.longevity: Not required for boost solenoid failure alone

problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt G16E-GTS Toyota GR Yaris engine prices

problems.h4: Cooling System & Water Pump Issues - Why the Toyota GR Yaris G16E-GTS Can Overheat
problems.typicalFailureMileage: Varies - more common on track-used vehicles
problems.rootCause: The G16E-GTS generates significant heat, particularly under track conditions. Water pump leakage and coolant reservoir leakage due to pressure buildup have been reported. Toyota addressed cooling concerns in the Gen 2 model by adding an additional sub-radiator and an intercooler water spray system as standard.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: If overheating has caused internal damage
repairOptions.longevity: Only if internal damage has occurred
